title: 3rd Stopping Place 3rd Truth The Truth Of Disposing And Administering

questions.question: What is the name of the Third Truth in the target passage?
questions.answer: It is the truth about Allah’s managing and running things.

questions.question: What kinds of things are included in this management?
questions.answer: It includes the huge bodies in the sky, the strong elements, and the weak creatures living on earth.

questions.question: According to the passage, how are these different things treated together?
questions.answer: They are made to help one another and are directed together in an orderly way.

questions.question: What examples are used to help us imagine the world under this rule?
questions.answer: The world is compared to a kingdom, a city, and a palace.

questions.question: Why does the passage use a comparison with a great commander?
questions.answer: It helps us understand how amazing it is to manage many different groups in perfect order.

questions.question: In the comparison, how many different groups are in the army?
questions.answer: There are four hundred thousand different groups.

questions.question: What does the commander provide for each group in the comparison?
questions.answer: He gives each group its own clothing, weapons, instructions, release, and pay.

questions.question: What would happen if an ordinary cause tried to interfere with that huge administration?
questions.answer: Order would be ruined and confusion would begin.

questions.question: In the real example on earth, what appears every spring?
questions.answer: A great living army of four hundred thousand different species appears.

questions.question: What happens in autumn to many plant and animal species?
questions.answer: Three hundred thousand of them are released from their duties and pass away.

questions.question: What is the main subject of the target passage?
questions.answer: It is about Allah’s perfect control and arrangement of creation.

questions.question: Which two opposite kinds of created things are mentioned to show the wide reach of this control?
questions.answer: Very great heavenly bodies and very weak earthly creatures are mentioned.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the way this control is carried out?
questions.answer: It says it is done with full order and balance.

questions.question: Why does the passage focus on spring on the face of the earth?
questions.answer: Because spring shows one clear page of this management that people can observe.

questions.question: In the comparison, what makes the commander’s work so amazing?
questions.answer: He manages many different groups separately and correctly without mistakes or delay.

questions.question: What idea is taught by saying no other cause could put its hand into that work?
questions.answer: It teaches that such complete order cannot come from many weak causes.

questions.question: What does the passage say we can see with our own eyes every spring?
questions.answer: We can see an unseen hand creating and directing a huge army of living species.

questions.question: How is autumn described in relation to the day of resurrection?
questions.answer: It is described as an example or reminder of it.

questions.question: What happens to the species in autumn?
questions.answer: Many of them are dismissed from their tasks and depart through death.

questions.question: What lesson about teamwork in creation comes from the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that different parts of creation are arranged to support one another under one rule.

questions.question: What title is given to the Third Truth?
questions.answer: It is called the truth of disposing and administering.

questions.question: What does “administering” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means managing, arranging, and taking care of everything properly.

questions.question: What three large pictures are used for the world in the passage?
questions.answer: A perfect kingdom, a splendid city, and a decorated palace.

questions.question: Why are heavenly bodies, natural elements, and earth’s creatures mentioned together?
questions.answer: They show that one system includes both the biggest and the smallest parts of the world.

questions.question: What season is chosen as a special example of this rule?
questions.answer: Spring is chosen.

questions.question: In the army comparison, what shows that each group is cared for in a special way?
questions.answer: Each one receives its own supplies and directions separately.

questions.question: What qualities mark the commander’s work in the comparison?
questions.answer: It is careful, fair, exact, timely, and free from mistakes.

questions.question: How many species are said to make up the spring army?
questions.answer: Four hundred thousand species.

questions.question: What season removes many of these species from duty?
questions.answer: Autumn does.

questions.question: Why is death described as a kind of leave from duty in the passage?
questions.answer: It presents living things as creatures serving for a time and then being released.

questions.question: What does the passage prove by showing so much order in such a huge number of living things?
questions.answer: It proves that one mighty and wise Lord is directing them.

questions.question: What truth is being explained in this part of the text?
questions.answer: It is the truth that Allah arranges and governs creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the movement and condition of the heavenly bodies?
questions.answer: They are huge and move swiftly.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the creatures living on earth?
questions.answer: They are needy and weak.

questions.question: How are all these different created things connected in the passage?
questions.answer: They are made to assist one another and are governed together.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the example about a world-ruling commander?
questions.answer: It is to show how hard it would be to manage countless different groups perfectly.

questions.question: Name two things the commander gives to every group.
questions.answer: He gives things like clothing and weapons.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the timing of this administration?
questions.answer: It happens at the right time without delay.

questions.question: If another power tried to join in this administration, what result would follow?
questions.answer: The balance would be broken and disorder would happen.

questions.question: What do people witness every spring, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They witness a great number of species being created and managed.

questions.question: How is autumn linked to resurrection in the passage?
questions.answer: It serves as a small likeness of the day when creatures are brought back and gathered.

questions.question: What does the phrase “disposing and administering” mainly point to?
questions.answer: It points to directing and organizing all things wisely.

questions.question: Which parts of creation are named to show the wide reach of this direction?
questions.answer: The skies, the elements, and the living beings on earth are named.

questions.question: What does the passage say is done for all these things besides simply creating them?
questions.answer: Their needs are handled and their affairs are arranged.

questions.question: How is the whole world pictured when this rule is described?
questions.answer: It is pictured as an excellently run realm and a beautifully ordered place.

questions.question: Why is the spring season a strong proof in this passage?
questions.answer: Because in spring many kinds of life appear together in careful order.

questions.question: In the comparison, why can’t random causes do the commander’s job?
questions.answer: Because the work is too vast, exact, and balanced for scattered causes.

questions.question: What number of different species is used in the spring example?
questions.answer: Four hundred thousand species.

questions.question: What happens to most of the species mentioned when autumn comes?
questions.answer: Three hundred thousand are sent away from their worldly duties.

questions.question: What does calling autumn a sample of resurrection teach us?
questions.answer: It teaches that the changing of seasons points to life after death.

questions.question: What is meant by an “unseen hand” creating and administering spring?
questions.answer: It means Allah is the One doing it, even though His action is not seen like a human hand.

questions.question: What is the heading of the Third Truth in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the truth of disposing and administering.

questions.question: What two qualities are named for the way this administration is done?
questions.answer: It is done with order and balance.

questions.question: Which powerful things are mentioned at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The great heavenly bodies and the strong natural elements are mentioned.

questions.question: Which vulnerable beings are mentioned along with them?
questions.answer: The weak and needy dwellers of the earth are mentioned.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens between these different parts of creation?
questions.answer: They are made to support each other.

questions.question: What three comparisons describe the world under this administration?
questions.answer: It is like a flawless kingdom, a great city, and a richly prepared palace.

questions.question: In the example of the commander, what shows perfect management?
questions.answer: Every group gets what it needs correctly, on time, and without confusion.

questions.question: Why would interference from any other cause fail?
questions.answer: Because it would upset the careful balance and create disorder.

questions.question: What does the passage say we clearly observe every spring?
questions.answer: We observe a huge living army of many different species being brought forth and directed.

questions.question: How many species are said to be dismissed in autumn?
questions.answer: Three hundred thousand species are dismissed.

questions.question: What does this passage teach about Allah’s control over the world?
questions.answer: It teaches that His control reaches everything, from the largest things to the weakest living creatures.
